title: Frank Cuny tuning bad pianos on jobs
summary: DeDroit says loving music is necessary for bad-piano jobs and tells how Cuny tuned pianos and played in the middle register.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: You don't know what a band leader goes to. You've got to be smiling when you feel like, you know. But after all, I think I'd do it again. Yeah? Yes, I loved it. And you've got to love music to play. You've got to love music to play in places where the piano is so bad that you turn the back of the piano to the people and tell the piano player, knock the head of note all night, and he sits there and gets his dope, how do you like that? If you ask him to tune the piano and they're $15 or $20, you don't want to spend it. Frank Cuny, my piano player, luckily for me that he could tune the pianos. He carried it. A tuning thing. You know what that big-

Tuning hammer. When we went in, we used to play at what is now Brennan's. That was called the Paddy O'Royle. Remember? Yeah. I was the most popular man with the manager because he knew he was going to get a new piano repair job.

The first thing he'd do is say, why are you all drinking? You know what I mean? And Cuny didn't drink. And Cuny used to be the reason why we used to, when we played on the courthouse steps during the Spring Fiesto, I had a big band, Fakin' in the dark, you know. Oh, come the way, it's a trip. You can't forget this, you know. A man said to me, he said, your piano player, he's on the piano more than he's on top of it. I said he's repairing the pedals now, he just got through with the keys. He tuned the piano. He said to me, look Johnny, no choruses tonight, and I'm going to play in the middle register. He'd stay in the middle register. He couldn't go here or there, because it was out of tune. And he wouldn't have time to tune the whole piano. So he'd tune the bad notes and the, you know. He'd be like, I know places. I played in Raceland one day, and that's a terrible place to play. They never tuned a piano ever. I played there and the piano was so bad that the saxes and the trumpets, we didn't have enough slide to pull out. And you play a whole lot of tunes. So I turned the back of the piano to the people. And I said, Frank, don't touch the piano. He said, that's easy. You know? So we played. Azure paid me. He said, good business. We did fine, Johnny. Come back again. I will. Al Streeman goes there. Al Streeman is the guy that sets up the band with white gloves on. He said, you know, he's not queer, but that kind of guy is. He refused to play the piano. The guy says to him, look, we had Johnny D. Droid here last week, and he saw there inside that and knew there was no compassion. He didn't come playing. So Streeman says, what did you do? I said, I didn't use it. He says, I wish. But he's the leader. They expect him to play the piano. Don't you see? He's the leader.
